prompt.adult: Matthew 1:23 gives the name the Son will be called. What does Matthew say that name is translated?
prompt.child: Matthew explains what the name given to Mary’s Son means. What does it mean?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 1:23, what does the name mean when translated?

verses.text: “Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and bear a Son, and they shall call His name Immanuel,” which is translated, “God with us.”

explanation.child: Look at the last words of Matthew 1:23.
explanation.teen: 1:23 gives the prophecy and then a translation. Read the translation.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:22 says all this was done that what the Lord spoke through the prophet might be fulfilled. 1:23 begins, “Behold, the virgin shall be with child.”
teaching.takeaway: The name is translated “God with us.”

prompt.adult: As Jesus drew near Jerusalem, at the Mount of Olives, what place did they come to before He sent two disciples?
prompt.child: On the way to Jerusalem, Jesus came near the Mount of Olives. What place did they reach?
prompt.teen: Matthew 21:1: “and came to” what place “at the Mount of Olives”?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 21:1, what place did they come to at the Mount of Olives?

verses.text: Now when they drew near Jerusalem, and came to Bethphage, at the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,

explanation.adult: Read the middle of 21:1, after “and came to.”
explanation.child: Look in the middle of Matthew 21:1.
explanation.teen: 21:1 names Jerusalem, then a place, then the Mount of Olives. Read the place in between.

teaching.extended_explanation: 21:1 ends with Jesus sending two disciples. 21:2 tells them what they will find tied in the village opposite.

prompt.adult: Matthew 2:17-18 quotes Jeremiah the prophet about a voice heard in Ramah. Lamentation and weeping are named. What else?
prompt.child: Matthew quotes Jeremiah about sad sounds heard in a town. Two are lamentation and weeping. What is the third?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 2:18, what is named with lamentation and weeping?

verses.text: Then was fulfilled what was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
“A voice was heard in Ramah, Lamentation, weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, Refusing to be comforted, Because they are no more.”

explanation.child: Look near the start of Matthew 2:18.
explanation.teen: 2:18 lists three sounds in a row. Read the last of the three.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:17 says this was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet. 2:18 goes on to say Rachel was refusing to be comforted.
teaching.takeaway: A voice was heard with “Lamentation, weeping, and great mourning.”

prompt.adult: When evening had come, many who were demon-possessed were brought to Jesus. According to 8:16, how did He cast out the spirits?
prompt.child: In the evening, people brought Jesus many who had evil spirits. How did He drive the spirits out?
prompt.teen: Matthew 8:16: “And He cast out the spirits” how?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 8:16, by what means did Jesus cast out the spirits?

verses.text: When evening had come, they brought to Him many who were demon-possessed. And He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick,
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying: “He Himself took our infirmities And bore our sicknesses.”

explanation.adult: Read the middle of 8:16, after “cast out the spirits.”
explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 16.
explanation.teen: 8:16 tells who was brought and then how He dealt with the spirits. Read the second part.
explanation.older: It follows “He cast out the spirits” in 8:16.

teaching.extended_explanation: 8:16 adds that He healed all who were sick. 8:17 says this fulfilled Isaiah: “He Himself took our infirmities And bore our sicknesses.”
teaching.takeaway: He cast out the spirits “with a word.”

prompt.adult: According to Matthew 4:12, what had Jesus heard when He departed to Galilee?
prompt.child: Jesus left for Galilee after He heard some news. What had He heard?
prompt.teen: Matthew 4:12: “Now when Jesus heard that” what?
prompt.older: Matthew 4:12-13 tells why Jesus moved to Galilee. What news had He heard?

choices.text: John had been put in prison
His family was looking for Him

verses.text: Now when Jesus heard that John had been put in prison, He departed to Galilee.
And leaving Nazareth, He came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the regions of Zebulun and Naphtali,

explanation.child: Look at the start of Matthew 4:12.
explanation.teen: 4:12 gives the news first and then where He went. Read the news.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:13 says He left Nazareth and dwelt by the sea, in the regions of Zebulun and Naphtali. 4:14 says this fulfilled what Isaiah the prophet had spoken.
teaching.takeaway: He heard that John had been put in prison.

prompt.adult: Matthew 8:17 says He took our infirmities. After He healed the great multitudes in chapter 12, what did He warn them in 12:16?
prompt.child: After Jesus healed large crowds, He gave them a warning. What did He warn them?
prompt.older: Linking Matthew 8:17 with 12:16, what did Jesus warn the healed multitudes?

choices.text: not to go to the temple

verses.text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying: “He Himself took our infirmities And bore our sicknesses.”
Yet He warned them not to make Him known,

explanation.child: Look at the last words of Matthew 12:16.
explanation.teen: 8:17 is the setting; 12:16 has one short warning. Read all of it after “warned them.”

teaching.extended_explanation: 8:17 quotes Isaiah about bearing sicknesses. 12:17 says this warning also fulfilled what Isaiah the prophet had spoken.
teaching.takeaway: He warned them “not to make Him known.”

prompt.adult: Matthew 21:5 tells the daughter of Zion that her King is coming. In 2:6, whom will the coming Ruler shepherd?
prompt.child: Matthew 2 quotes a prophet about a Ruler who would come. Whom would He shepherd?
prompt.older: Alongside the King of 21:5, whom does 2:6 say the Ruler will shepherd?

verses.text: ‘But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, Are not the least among the rulers of Judah; For out of you shall come a Ruler Who will shepherd My people Israel.’ ”
“Tell the daughter of Zion, ‘Behold, your King is coming to you, Lowly, and sitting on a donkey, A colt, the foal of a donkey.’ ”

explanation.child: Look at the last words of Matthew 2:6.
explanation.teen: 21:5 is the setting; 2:6 ends with the Ruler’s task. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 21:5 says the King is coming to the daughter of Zion, sitting on a donkey. 2:6 calls the coming one a Ruler.
teaching.takeaway: The Ruler “will shepherd My people Israel.”

prompt.adult: Matthew 2:17 opens a word spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, and so does 27:9. According to 27:10, for what were the coins given?
prompt.child: Matthew says the money paid for Jesus was later used to buy something. What was it for?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 27:10, what were the coins given for, as the LORD directed?

verses.text: Then was fulfilled what was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
and gave them for the potter’s field, as the LORD directed me.”

explanation.child: Look at the start of Matthew 27:10.
explanation.teen: 2:17 is the setting; 27:10 says where the coins went and then who directed it. Read the first part.
explanation.older: It follows “and gave them for” in 27:10.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:17 introduces the voice heard in Ramah. 27:10 ends, “as the LORD directed me.”
teaching.takeaway: They gave them “for the potter’s field.”
